summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted for confusion and reported bloody stools. His symptoms were attributed to hepatic encephalopathy, likely due to noncompliance with lactulose, with rapid improvement after restarting treatment. Evaluation for gastrointestinal bleeding showed no active bleed on guaiac testing or nasogastric lavage, and hematocrit remained stable. A preliminary blood culture showed coagulase-negative staph, but repeat cultures were negative, ruling out infection. He was discharged home with increased lactulose, addition of omeprazole, and adjustments to other medications, including reduced fluoxetine and tamoxifen doses. He was alert, oriented, and hemodynamically stable at discharge.
